To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) DCCs are a natural outcome of high-energy collisions in the theory of the strong interactions, and their detection would constitute a discovery of a new phase of matter; (ii) the DCCs are expected to be produced in ultra-high energy cosmic rays, and (iii) the DCC signal can be identified by a significant asymmetry between the neutral and charged pion fractions in cosmic ray showers, as reflected in the X max and muon number observables.

(1) the neutral-to-chared pion ratio is not a good observable, since it is not very sensitive to the neutral-to-charge pion asymmetry, (2) the number of muons is a better observable, and (3) the depth of the shower maximum is a better observable.

(i) the neutral-to-chared pion fraction asymmetries in DCC events can be detected in X max measurements; (ii) the muon number on the ground is sensitive to the neutral-to-charge pion fraction asymetry in the DCC events; (iii) the neutral-to-chaarged pion fraction is not correlated with the muon number; (iv) the muon numbers in the DCC and the non-DCC events are correlated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the search for the DCCs in cosmic ray showers.
the possibility that DCCs are produced in the primary interactions of ultra-high energy nuclei with the atmosphere.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present experimental data on cosmic ray showers cannot exclude the formation of DCCs in the interactions of ultra-high energy protons with the cosmic radiation background.
the current experimental results do not allow us to draw any firm conclusions about the existence of DCCs in cosmic ray interactions.
DCCs are not excluded, but also not required, by current data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, if DCCs are produced in cosmic ray showers, the neutral pion asymmetry is likely to be large enough to be detected with the present and near-future experiments.
the X max distribution shows the most promise to reveal DCCs, but that the muon number on the ground is not a useful observable for this purpose.
the neutral-to-chared pion asymmetries in DCCs are too small to be detected in cosmic ray showers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DCCs can be searched for in the cosmic ray data by means of a simple observable, namely the ratio of X max to the depth of the shower maximum expected from a pure pion shower.
the muon component of cosmic ray showers is a very promising tool to search for DCCs.
the neutral-to-charg pion asymmetry is a robust signature of DCC formation, which can be searched for in future measurements of the cosmic ray composition at the Pierre Auger Observatory.
